title: How Matt Pocock uses Claude Code for real engineering: plan mode, multi-phase plans, GitHub issues
summary: Matt walks through building a CLI feature with Claude Code. He starts in plan mode, answers clarifying questions, splits the work into phases, stores the plan as a GitHub issue, and clears context between phases. His memory file keeps replies concise and ends each plan with unresolved questions.

principles.text: Start big work in plan mode so the agent explores the codebase and asks clarifying questions before writing code.
principles.quote: Whenever I embark out on a big piece of work, I'm always thinking about creating a plan first.

principles.text: Tell the agent to be extremely concise in every interaction; it makes plans easy to read.
principles.quote: in all interactions and commit messages, be extremely concise and sacrifice grammar for the sake of concision.

principles.text: Have each plan end with a list of unresolved questions so you can answer them before execution.
principles.quote: at the end of each plan, give me a list of unresolved questions to answer, if any, and again, make the questions extremely concise.

principles.text: Break large plans into phases so work can span multiple context windows without overrunning the LLM.
principles.quote: if this piece of work is too large, it's going to overrun the context window of the LLM. It's going to be much better going forward if I break this into a multi-phase plan

principles.text: Do heavy upfront planning, then run execution with auto-accept edits; review the diff at the end of each phase.
principles.quote: Now that we've done the planning, we can be pretty aggressive with accept edits on because we understand the implementation a bit and we kind of get what's going on.

principles.text: Store the multi-phase plan as a GitHub issue so it survives context resets and teammates can comment async.
principles.quote: I really like keeping these assets in the cloud because then actually people can comment on them, add stuff overnight, add stuff async.
